2. Senior Advocate Mr. Nirupam Nanavaty appearing with R/CR.MA/8202/2022 ORDER DATED:
20/04/2023 learned advocate Mr. Premal Rachh for the applicants submitted that essentially,
applicant - Pooja Hiranandani who is an employee of SRC, i.e. Sindhu Resettlement Corporation Pooja Chandubhai Hirananadani vs State Of Gujarat on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170394928/
1 Limited, whereas other two accused / applicants namely, Dipti Dharmeshbhai Aashar and Ratilal Ravjibhai Solanki were the persons who were inducted as partners of Spark Hospitality & Events LLP and the dispute is related to account as SRC gave contract to the complainant to run a club owned by SRC.

entities.text: Sindhu Resettlement Corporation Pooja Chandubhai Hirananadani vs State Of Gujarat

sentences.text:
Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Nanavaty, by relying upon the document produced at page 55 which is a communication dated 30.3.2022 by Senior Executive Engineer of SRC to the Police Inspector, Gandhidham A Division Police Station submitted that by way of this communication, SRC which is the employer of applicant - Pooja Hiranandani has categorically stated that the firm has deposited the outstanding dues from their bank account and one Mr.
Subhash Swami and two other applicants of this application were carrying out the business in the said premises.

Learned Senior Advocate also submitted that there is one arbitration proceeding also going on between SRC and original complainant and he also submitted that as the amount R/CR.MA/8202/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 under dispute has already been deposited by the erstwhile partners even that ground is not available to the original complainant.

Learned Senior Advocate further submitted that the interim orders dated 04.05.2022 and 01.06.2022 passed by coordinate bench of this Court whereby interim relief was granted in favour of the present applicants is self-explanatory and pursuant to that orders, each of the applicants had remained present before the Investigating Officer and they have cooperated and they are cooperating and even in future also and they have also submitted necessary documents to the Investigating Officer.
Learned

Senior Advocate further submitted that out of three applicants, two applicants are lady accused / applicants and considering the fact that they have already cooperated with the investigation and now there is no point of arresting them and seeking custodial interrogation.
Learned advocate, therefore, submitted that considering the above facts, the applicants may be granted anticipatory bail.

3. Learned advocate Mr. Zubin Bharda appearing with learned advocate Mr. Dhruvik K. Patel for respondent No.1 vehemently opposed this application and submitted that it is one R/CR.MA/8202/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 of the accused / applicants, i.e. Pooja Hiranandani who was an employee of SRC, however, from the account of Spark Hospitality & Events LLP, in which the original complainant was inducted as partner.

There are monetary transactions to the tune of Rs.71 lakh and during the course of hearing, he has also submitted a chart indicating the amounts transferred from the aforesaid account of Spark Hospitality & Events LLP to the account of mother of present applicant No.1, i.e. Pooja Hiranandani.

Learned advocate Mr. Bharda further submitted that there are cash vouchers which would indicate that the amount was siphoned and the present applicants have played an active role in that and, therefore, they may not be granted anticipatory bail.
Learned advocate Mr. Bharda further submitted that the arbitration proceedings are between the complainant and SRC and the present applicants have nothing to do with those arbitration proceedings.
4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

Learned APP produced a report dated 20.04.2023 submitted by Police R/CR.MA/8202/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 Inspector, Local Crime Branch, East Kachchh - Gandhidham, which is taken on record and as per the aforesaid report, the complaint of the complainant is not supported by any evidence and as such there is no forged agreement found or at the end of preliminary investigation, it is not a case of Pooja Chandubhai Hirananadani vs State Of Gujarat on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170394928/
2 siphoning made out.
5.

sentences.text: I have heard learned advocates for the parties and have inquired from the learned advocate for the applicants that though an amount of more than Rs.71 lakh has been alleged to have been siphoned whether any civil remedy has been existed or not.
However, learned advocate Mr. Bharda fairly submitted that for one or other reason, civil remedy could not be existed.

6. Having heard the learned advocates for the parties and perusing the material placed on record and taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations, gravity of offences, role attributed to the accused, without discussing the evidence in detail, at this stage, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicants.

In the facts and circumstances of the present case, since the custodial interrogation of the applicants is not required, I R/CR.MA/8202/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 am inclined to consider the case of the applicants.

9. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors., reported at [2011] 1 SCC 694, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court reiterated the law laid down by the Constitution Bench in the case of Shri Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab, reported at (1980) 2 SCC 565.
10.
